Split-KV Paged Attention Decode — official score 0.5339

Split-KV Paged Attention Decode — official score 0.5339
Memory summary

The final solution uses a hand-written CUDA C++ split-KV decode kernel, compiled through PyTorch load_inline. It passed the official correctness check and scored 0.5339 peak_fraction on the RTX PRO 6000, above the benchmark’s 0.1 OK threshold. The audit labels the run interesting and records the score as 0.534.

Relevant prior context

The run inspected the reference, checker, benchmark, and project layout, then probed the GPU and compiler before implementing the kernel. The final reconstructed code is U007_solution.py; the available U003 through U007 files are identical.

The kernel assigns one CTA to each (batch, KV head, sequence chunk). Eight warps stream pages round-robin. Each warp maintains independent online-softmax streams, then merges them through shared memory. For multi-chunk cases, the first kernel writes fp32 output and (max, sum) partials; a second kernel rescales and reduces the chunks. When one chunk suffices, the first kernel writes bf16 output directly.

A useful register-saving detail is that the same qacc register array holds scaled query values in K lanes and the V accumulator in V lanes. Packed [K | V] rows are read with 128-bit-per-lane warp loads. Chunk count is chosen to target roughly two CTAs per SM across the GPU’s 188 SMs.

Smoke tests covered all five benchmark shapes, including sequence length 1535 and head dimension 64. The official check then returned:

PASS
